newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian child murder report slams police rivalry.
newsitem.headline: Belgian child murder report slams police rivalry.

text.p: A string of kidnapped, raped and murdered Belgian children might have been rescued if police and magistrates had worked with, not against, each other, according to a special report published on Tuesday.

The scandal has shaken Belgium to the core since it broke eight months ago with the discovery of the bodies of four abducted, abused and murdered young girls. A fifth dead girl was found last month, and police are still looking for others.
"If the right decisions had been taken in 1995, the children would without doubt have been found, perhaps alive," the report by a special parliamentary commission said.
"There was a flagrant failure to pass information between the prosecutors and the police," Commission member Nathalie de 'T Serclaes told parliament.
In October more than 250,000 people marched through Brussels, in sympathy with the victims and their parents and in a show of disgust at a system seen by most as incompetent and by some as corrupt.

Convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux has been charged with murder, businessman Michel Nihoul has been charged as an accomplice and, in another case, convicted child molester Patrick Derochette has been charged with rape leading to death.

The report spares no one in its scathing description of rivalry between the country's three different police forces and lackadaisical magistrates, but suggests that sheer incompetence might not be the sole explanation.
"The commission finds it difficult not to conclude, based on relevant evidence, that Nihoul, Dutroux, Derochette and their accomplices may have been protected," the report said.

Investigators were slow to get onto the cases, ignored vital evidence, were cold and dismissive towards the parents, jealously guarded key information, had insufficient resources and used them badly and in a completely uncoordinated manner, it said.

The report follows six months of often televised hearings after Dutroux led police in August first to the bodies of eight-year-olds Julie Lejeune and Melissa Russo, and then to those of teenagers An Marchal and Eefje Lambrecks.
Last month the body of eight-year-old Belgian-born Moroccan girl Loubna Benaissa was found stuffed into a steel trunk in the basement of a Brussels garage near her home.
Derochette has been charged with illegal imprisonment and rape leading to her death.
The father of An and the father and elder sister of Loubna were in a packed parliament for the presentation of the report, which will be debated on Thursday and Friday.

The fact that Nihoul organised orgies and had close contacts with the police, and that the gendarmerie were running a surveillance operation against Dutroux but still failed to stop him, has added fuel to the protection theory.

"The malfunctioning of the Belgian penal system today poses serious problems that put at grave risk the state of law," the commission said, proposing creation of gle, federal police force to replace the existing three.

"But if the commisssion has been able to establish the causes, it has not yet been able to determine the reasons. The commission will therefore dedicate itself to this task during the second phase of its work," it continued.
"It cannot exclude, in this respect, that the malfunctions were linked to possible protections," the report concluded.
The commission will now work on this hypothesis until September 30. This second report will be keenly watched by the Belgian public.
